requirements.requirement: Limit account datauser to 100 MB of storage under /srv/data, enforced by the filesystem.
requirements.summary: A dedicated XFS filesystem is persistently mounted at /srv/data with user-quota enforcement. datauser has 100M soft and hard block limits, and direct writes by that account were stopped with “Disk quota exceeded.” After restart, the mount and quota returned, the persistent marker remained intact, and enforcement was demonstrated again. Temporary test files were removed.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: The system remained CentOS Stream 10 with kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 before and after configuration and restart. The solution used the platform's available XFS tooling, and final package-health checks remained successful.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, restart was acknowledged, the connection disruption was observed, a different boot identity appeared, and system, mount, account, data, quota, and enforcement state recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Account, directory, backing-image, filesystem, fstab, mount, ownership, quota, and permission changes all contributed directly to the required filesystem quota. The initial mkfs invocation used an overlong label, but its created account, directories, and backing image were retained and used by the corrected final implementation, so it was not an unrelated experiment. Quota-test files and error files were removed. The persistent marker and scheduled restart served bounded restart evidence. Final observations show no failed services, no new network exposure, healthy package state, and only expected reboot-related PID and systemd-private-directory changes.
